title: Can't be done
goal: Read and write notices with voices and ability (yapılamaz, çözülebilir), and recognize double causatives such as öldürtmek.

intro.text: After the voices come negation and ability: *yap-ıl-abil-ir* (it can be done), *yap-ıl-a-maz* (it can't be done). A second causative adds another person: *öldürtmek* (to have someone killed); in speech, *kestirttim* often just means *kestirdim*.

vocab.en: to solve; to untie, to undo
to force; to push, to strain
special; private; personal (özel olarak: especially, specially)
order (for goods); sipariş vermek: to order

exercises.question: *Bu kapı içeriden açılamaz.* What does the sign say?
options: This door can't be opened from the inside.
Don't open this door from the inside.
This door is never opened from the inside.

why.1: An order would be *Bu kapıyı içeriden açmayınız*.
why.2: That would be the plain aorist passive, *açılmaz*, without inability.

exercises.explain: *aç-ıl-a-maz*: passive, then inability *-a-ma*, in the aorist: **can't be opened**.

exercises.text: Merak etme, bu sorun kolayca çöz___.
exercises.en: Don't worry, this problem can easily be solved.

reject.why: *Çözebilir* is **he can solve**. The problem itself **can be solved**: passive first, *çöz-ül-ebil-ir*.
*Çözülür* is **it gets solved**. For **can be**, add `-(y)Abil`: *çözülebilir*.

exercises.label: *seçilebilmek*, aorist: I can be elected, you can be elected…

exercises.explain: After l the passive is `-In`: *bul-un-*. Then inability *-a-ma* and the past *-dı*.

exercises.prompt: This medicine can't be bought without a prescription.
accept: Bu ilaç reçete olmadan satın alınamaz.

reject.why: *Alamaz* is **he can't buy**. The medicine **can't be bought**: *al-ın-a-maz*.
*Alınmaz* is a rule, **isn't bought**. **Can't be bought** adds inability: *alınamaz*.

exercises.explain: *al-ın-a-maz*: after l the passive is `-In`, then inability in the aorist.

accept: The meeting can't be postponed, everyone has to come.
The meeting can't be postponed everyone must come.
The meeting can't be postponed so everyone has to come.
The meeting can't be postponed so everyone must come.
The meeting can't be put off everyone has to come.
The meeting can't be put off everyone must come.
The meeting can't be put off so everyone has to come.
The meeting can't be put off so everyone must come.

exercises.en: Unfortunately, there's nothing to be done.

exercises.question: *Padişah veziri öldürttü.* Who killed the vizier?
options: No one: the vizier died of illness

why.1: That would be *öldürdü*. The second causative *-t* brings in someone else who did it.
why.2: *Öldürmek* is **to kill**; the sentence is about a killing ordered by the sultan.

exercises.explain: *öl-dür-t-tü*: *öldürmek* (to kill) + a second causative: **had him killed**.

exercises.question: In everyday speech, *Saçımı kestirttim* means the same as…

why.2: *Kesildi* is a passive: it says nothing about who wanted it done.

exercises.explain: In speech, *kestirttim* is often just *kestirdim*, **I had my hair cut**. In writing, keep one causative.

exercises.prompt: Your order can be delivered on Monday.

reject.why: *Teslim edebilir* is **he can deliver**. The order **can be delivered**: *teslim ed-il-ebil-ir*.

exercises.explain: *teslim et-* → passive *edil-* (t softens to d before the vowel) → *edilebilir*.

exercises.text: A special mould can be made for you.
accept: A special mold can be made for you.

exercises.en: The lost bag just couldn't be found.

accept: This part can't easily be replaced.
This part can't be replaced easily.
This part can't easily be changed.
This part can't be changed easily.
This part is not easy to replace.
